title: Bradley Whitford on Bringing Back ‘The West Wing’ as a ‘Limited Series’
description:
Bradley Whitford is ready to return to the White House.

	The actor tells me that it may be time to bring back “The West Wing” as a “limited series
body:
Bradley Whitford is ready to return to the White House.

	The actor tells me that it may be time to bring back “The West Wing” as a “limited series of some kind.”

	Series creator Aaron Sorkin has had fans chomping at the bit ever since he told Variety’s Michael Schneider he was inspired to write more episodes while attending a 25th anniversary of the show at the White House in 2024. “I just got a couple of ideas for episodes just walking around the White House,” Sorkin said at the time. “Like, ‘why didn’t we ever do this? Why didn’t we ever do that?’”
	

	Whitford inspired a “West Wing” reunion earlier today when his fellow castmates Martin Sheen, Dulé Hill, Mary McCormack and Josh Malina joined him at the unveiling of his star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.


	“I’ll work him, I’ll work him,” Whitford said of trying to get Sorkin to commit.


	Hill said the cast wouldn’t hesitate if Sorkin decides to write a new season. “I always say that’s a question for Aaron Sorkin,” he said when asked about a revival. “If he writes it, then I will come. I think if he writes it, then we all will be there.”

	However, Hill continued, “Sometimes I wonder though where things are in the world. Things are so outlandish, I don’t know how you dramatize any of that. With him writing, it would be a lovely thing to hopefully steer the collective consciousness of our society back toward humanity and connectivity and understanding.”

Dulé Hill says the “West Wing” cast is ready to return if Aaron Sorkin decides to write a new season: “We all will be there.”via Bradley Whitford’s Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony pic.twitter.com/xde3oQceuY— Variety (@Variety) September 30, 2026


	“The West Wing” premiered on NBC in 1999 and ran for seven seasons before ending in 2006. The ensemble also included Rob Lowe, Allison Janney, Richard Schiff, John Spencer, Janel Moloney and Stockard Channing.
	

	The series won 27 Emmy Awards from 95 nominations.

title: Nicolas Cage Says the Marvel Cinematic Universe ‘Is Becoming a Well-Funded and Glorified WWE’ With 50-Plus Year Olds in ‘Ridiculous Outfits’
description: Nicolas Cage‘s critique of the Marvel Cinematic Universe during a recent conversation at Fan Expo Dallas (via The Playlist) is quickly gaining tract
body:
Nicolas Cage‘s critique of the Marvel Cinematic Universe during a recent conversation at Fan Expo Dallas (via The Playlist) is quickly gaining traction on social media, with many people either agreeing with the Oscar-winning actor or questioning him considering his own ties to superhero projects. 

	“I do say this with love,” Cage said at the convention. “When I see these 50-plus and otherwise intelligent and remarkably gifted thespians putting on these ridiculous outfits and getting ready for the fight — let’s face it, it’s all cutting to the fight — it’s hard for me not to be reminded that the MCU is becoming a well-funded and glorified WWE.”
	

	Cage is not a member of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, although he just played the title character in Sony’s Marvel series “Spider-Noir.” The show was canceled after one season, which consisted of eight episodes. Cage also played the Marvel superhero Ghost Rider in two movies, 2007’s “Ghost Rider” and 2012’s “Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance,” and now the comic book character is officially joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe courtesy of Ryan Gosling. The MCU’s “Ghost Rider,” directed by Shawn Levy, is on the release calendar for July 28, 2028.


	Cage’s “Spider-Noir” series was based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man Noir and was adapted for television by Oren Uziel. The series took place during the Great Depression and starred Cage as Ben Reilly, “a seasoned, down-on-his-luck private investigator in 1930s New York, who is forced to grapple with his past life following a deeply personal tragedy, as the city’s one and only superhero.”
	

	Speaking to Variety before the show’s premiere, Cage said he was attracted to “Spider-Noir” not because of its superhero roots but because the show was being designed in black and white as a classic film noir (and thus with shades of German expressionism thrown in). 

	“I wanted to try to create an essence of some of my favorite old world actors because I wanted to embody that style — Bogart, Cagney, Edward G. Robinson — and designed my performance to fit within the black-and-white format,” Cage said, adding that taking on a television show made him nervous at first.

	“It was scary, and it was risky,” he continued. “I was constantly worried that I was going to get fired, because I was doing this thing of channeling old actors and colliding it with Stan Lee’s masterpiece that is ‘Spider-Man’ to create this Roy Lichtenstein pop-art sensation of sorts. I didn’t know until I finally saw the eight episodes whether it was going to work.”

title: Box Office: ‘Verity’ Aims for $35 Million Debut and Anne Hathaway’s Third No. 1 Movie of the Year, ‘Digger’ Could Bomb With $12 Million
description: Anne Hathaway is returning to a familiar spot — the top of box office charts — as “Verity” hits the big screen over the weekend. The adaptation of C
body:
Anne Hathaway is returning to a familiar spot — the top of box office charts — as “Verity” hits the big screen over the weekend. The adaptation of Colleen Hoover’s bestseller is targeting a solid domestic debut of $30 million to $35 million from 3,510 theaters, which should be enough to register as Hathaway’s third No. 1 opening of the year. She also starred in this summer’s blockbusters “The Devil Wears Prada 2″ and “The Odyssey.”
	

	In a twist that few might have predicted this time last year, “Verity” will tower over Tom Cruise and Alejandro González Iñárritu’s R-rated environmental satire “Digger,” which also debuts this weekend. The big-budget film is shaping up to be one of the year’s biggest bombs, with opening weekend projections of $12 million to $15 million from 3,300 North American screens.


	“Verity” is the latest of Hoover’s works to get the big-screen treatment following Sony’s 2024 sleeper hit “It Ends With Us,” Paramount’s 2025 drama “Regretting You” and Universal’s 2026 romance “Reminders of Him.” Among her adaptations, “It Ends With Us” landed the biggest debut with $50 million, followed by “Reminders of Him” with $17 million and “Regretting You” with $13.6 million. “It Ends With Us” is the highest-grossing of the trio by far with $350 million globally. Hoover’s film adaptations have modest budgets, making them low-risk bets for studios.


	“Verity” was produced for $40 million and will help Amazon MGM rebound after this summer’s “Masters of the Universe,” which flopped with $113 million globally against a $200 million budget. Amazon MGM, a relative newcomer to theatrical, delivered its first major win in the spring with Ryan Gosling’s astronaut drama “Project Hail Mary,” which grossed $684 million globally. Later this year, the studio has “I Play Rocky,” a crowd pleaser about the making of the 1976 Sylvester Stallone classic “Rocky,” and the heist thriller “How to Rob a Bank” with Nicholas Hoult and Pete Davidson.
	

	Hathaway, who also starred in this year’s psychodrama “Mother Mary” and sci-fi thriller “The End of Oak Street,” shares the screen in “Verity” with Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett. Directed by Michael Showalter (“The Big Sick”), the movie centers around famed author Verity Crawford, who gets badly injured in a car accident, leaving her husband to hire a struggling writer to complete the remaining books in the popular series. Reviews have been mixed, with Variety’s Guy Lodge calling “Verity” a “listless” and “unintentionally funny tale.”

	“Digger” looks to continue a dismal year for Warner Bros. — having fielded such misfires as “The Bride!” and “Supergirl” — and the timing couldn’t be worse. Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. is set to close next week. For Warners, it’s a stark reversal in fortunes from the studio’s 2025 slate, which boasted an unprecedented string of commercial triumphs including “Sinners,” “A Minecraft Movie” and “Weapons.”

	“Digger” was greenlit at Warner Bros. for $125 million, but according to four knowledgeable sources, the budget climbed to $160 million to $180 million after production went over schedule. A Warner Bros. spokesperson disputes those figures. Box office experts say a movie of this size would need a debut near $40 million to justify its price tag.

	Cruise stars in “Digger” as a wealthy oil tycoon whose company causes a potential catastrophe. Reviews and word-of-mouth have been so negative that Warner Bros. has started to embrace the bad press. In a new ad, the studio told moviegoers to “decide for yourself” after critics bashed the movie as “unpleasant” and “baffling.”

title: Colleen Hoover's 'Verity' Returns to Top of Book Charts on Heels of Movie Adaptation Release
description:

	Author Co
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Author Colleen Hoover‘s 2018 romantic thriller, “Verity,” is back on the bestsellers chart as a motion picture adaptation of the novel hits theaters nationwide.

	The hardcover version of “Verity” is currently number two on Amazon’s bestselling books chart, just behind the new Rebecca Yarros release, “Threshing Day,” which is the fourth book in the author’s “Empyrean” series. “Verity” is also number two on the Audible audiobook charts (as of this writing), back near the top after more than 100 weeks on the list.


	“Verity” was an instant hit with readers when it was first released, and quickly became a #1 New York Times Bestseller and BookTok favorite.

		

						
			
	

					Amazon
	
					
		

										COLLECTOR’S EDITION						

					Verity		

	
		Amazon currently has the book on sale for 30% off, with a “collector’s edition” that includes an exclusive new chapter from Hoover, as well as a new author’s letter.	
		
	

	From publishers Grand Central Publishing, the 368-page book follows struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh, who takes a job working for Jeremy Crawford, the husband of bestselling author Verity Crawford, who is presumed to be comatose after a car accident. Ashleigh is asked to help finish Verity’s book series, and soon begins pouring over manuscripts to piece the books together. But as the publisher notes state, “What Lowen doesn’t expect to uncover in the chaotic office is an unfinished autobiography Verity never intended for anyone to read―page after page of bone-chilling admissions, including Verity’s recollection of the night her family was forever altered.”

		

						
			
	

					Amazon
	
					
		

										LISTEN TO THE AUDIOBOOK						

					Verity [Audiobook]		

	
		You can also listen to the audiobook version of “Verity” by streaming or downloading it on Audible. The audiobook is available for purchase or you can listen to it free online with a free trial to Audible here.	
		
	

	“Verity” has now been adapted into a movie starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett. The film was first announced last March and hits theaters Oct. 2.

	“Verity” was self-published by Hoover in 2018 before being acquired by Grand Central Publishing in 2021. The film adaptation comes on the heels of “It Ends With Us,” the Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni-starring film which was also based on a Hoover book.


	You can find other versions of “Verity” and read all of Hoover’s books online on Amazon.com.

title: How to Watch F1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia Race Online for Free
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	The 2026
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	The 2026 Formula 1 season takes a bit of a detour this weekend as the drivers head to the F1 Bahrain Grand Prix — but not in actual Bahrain.

	The annual race in the Kingdom of Bahrain has been moved to Malaysia for this weekend, following uncertainties in the Middle East triggered by President Trump’s war in Iran. Now officially known as the “2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia,” the race takes place this Sunday, Oct. 4 live from the Sepang International Circuit in the Southeast Asian country.


	The official starting time for the Bahrain Grand Prix is at 3 p.m. Malaysia time (3 a.m. ET/12 a.m. PT). Apple TV is the official U.S. streaming home for Formula 1 and viewers can tune into the race through the Apple TV website or app (Amazon Prime members can also add Apple TV to their streaming channels here).

	While Apple TV now costs $14.99/month after a recent price hike, this weekend’s F1 race is free to watch online on the streamer. Fans can watch the practice rounds, qualifying and Sunday’s race online for free, with no subscription required. Apple says the race weekend is part of Apple TV’s previously announced plan to make select races and practice sessions available free to fans throughout the season.

	Apple TV is streaming the F1 Bahrain Grand Prix in 4K with Dolby Vision and immersive 5.1 surround sound. Note: you’ll need a streaming device that supports 4K content in order to get the 4K feed.

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

										NEWEST MODEL						

					Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max		

	
		Amazon’s Fire TV Stick offers 4K streaming with support for Dolby Vision plus the ability to look up content and control settings with the voice remote.	
		
	

	Continue on with Apple TV at the $14.99/month rate after the race is over or test-drive the streamer with a 7-day free trial here before committing.


	The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia follows a dramatic photo-finish between Mercedes star George Russell and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in Azerbaijan last week. Current Drivers’ Championship leader Kimi Antonelli finished fifth, further padding his lead in the standings over teammate Russell.

	The drivers head to Malaysia this weekend to tackle the 5.5-kilometer Sepang International Circuit, which hosted the Formula 1 Malaysian Grand Prix from 1999 to 2017.

	The race also comes on the heels of the latest F1 x Disney merch drop, with apparel and accessories inspired by racing motifs, Mickey Mouse and the hit Pixar movie, “Cars.”

		

						
			
	

					DisneyStore
	
					
		

										OFFICIAL MERCH						

					Formula 1 x Disney Collection		

	
		You can shop the officially-licensed collection online now at DisneyStore.	
		
	

	Livestream the 2026 F1 Malaysia race online free through Apple TV here.

title: Golden Globes Predictions: Let the Genre Games Begin for ‘Obsession,’ ‘Michael,’ ‘Wildwood’ and More
description: Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predi
body:
Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.



	

					Zendaya in “Dune Part Three”
									Warner Bros.
	




	Golden Globes Predictions Commentary (Updated: Sept. 30, 2026): The Golden Globes submission deadline is coming up on Oct. 30, the night before Halloween. Fitting, since for the next 30 days, studios get to decide what costume their movies should wear for the early phase of awards season.

	The Globes split their top film prize into two genres, drama and comedy/musical and the line between them has always been drawn by strategy as much as tone. Remember, this is the same awards show that “The Martian” once won best comedy.

	For the third year in a row, the comedy/musical side looks more competitive than its drama counterpart. We’re used to seeing it the other way around, and several major players still haven’t declared.

	On the drama side, Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster “The Odyssey” and “La Bola Negra,” the acclaimed epic from Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (better known as Los Javis), lead the early pack. The Netflix title picked up the People’s Choice Award at the Toronto International Film Festival this month, four months after the duo won best director at Cannes. That bodes well for its run.

	The race is still waiting on first reviews for a couple of contenders in the wings. Sources tell Variety that Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three” held its first intimate, small-group screenings this past week. Early word is very positive.

	And on Friday, the New York Film Festival unveils Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!” as its centerpiece selection, with Pedro Pascal as a former child prodigy cellist. Searchlight releases it Dec. 4, and it could make for an interesting addition to the race.

	No studio has a trickier sorting job than Amazon MGM Studios this year. It holds three contenders that could all plausibly claim the drama side: Phil Lord and Chris Miller’s “Project Hail Mary” with Ryan Gosling, Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky,” which finished first runner-up for TIFF’s People’s Choice Award and Bassam Tariq’s critically acclaimed “Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother,” the Orion Pictures release starring Mahershala Ali as a devout hitman.

	“Your Mother” is all but certain to run in drama. So expect at least one of the other two to go the comedy route, if only to keep the studio from splitting its own vote. Our bet is “Hail Mary” goes comedy, and “Rocky” goes drama.

	Focus Features has a choice to make with “Obsession,” Curry Barker’s micro-budget possession thriller that has grossed more than $400 million worldwide. If the studio follows the “Get Out” (2017) and “The Substance” (2024) playbooks, many expect a comedy push. But assess the landscape, especially for breakout star Inde Navarrette, who looks primed for a best actress Oscar nom as a possessed young woman and this pundit starts to wonder — wouldn’t a drama run make more sense?

	“Obsession” will likely find recognition in cinematic and box office achievement, and Navarrette should be nominated on either side of the house. Its best picture prospects face far steeper hurdles. I think the real question is where can she win?



	

					Sandra Hüller in “Fatherland” and “Rose”
									Mubi
	



	Drama actress is less stacked than usual. The only presumed threat to win is Sandra Hüller, who arrives with a double dose of Paweł Pawlikowski’s “Fatherland” and Markus Schleinzer’s “Rose,” which earned her the best leading performance prize in Berlin. On the comedy side, most pundits and analysts see the trophy as preordained for Julianne Moore’s towering work in Jesse Eisenberg’s beloved “The Debut.” Navarrette would also have to contend with Olivia Wilde in “The Invite,” a film poised to be a big player across the board.

	A drama win would position the 25-year-old Latina breakout as the alternative to Moore, and recent history shows what that moment can do. In each of the past two years, a Globes lead drama winner was someone the Actor Awards (formerly SAG) had passed over: Fernanda Torres for “I’m Still Here” and Wagner Moura for “The Secret Agent.” Both used the win as a springboard into nomination voting and landed Oscar noms. SAG voters have long been resistant to non-English-language performances. Let Hüller, whose two contenders are both in German, walk away with drama actress and she inherits that narrative. 

	Antoine Fuqua’s “Michael,” starring Jaafar Jackson and the first biopic ever to cross $1 billion worldwide, is also awaiting an official decision and it can go either way based on Globes history. “Bohemian Rhapsody” (2018) and Baz Luhrmann’s “Elvis” (2022) were embraced as dramas, and both won lead actor there. “Ray” (2004) and “Walk the Line” (2005) went comedy/musical and did the same. Among other music-driven films, “A Star Is Born” (2018) found love as a drama, while “Inside Llewyn Davis” (2013) went comedy. There’s no rhyme or reason, so anything can happen. We think a comedy/musical run is ultimately in the cards for “Michael,” alongside a run in cinematic and box office achievement. But again, anything can still happen.

	Speaking of box office, what many may not realize is that films must officially submit for the category. Nothing lands on the ballot automatically, and at the 2025 Globes, Villeneuve’s team opted to keep “Dune: Part Two” out of the box office race and vie only for best picture (drama), where it landed a nomination.

	We’re keeping that in mind for the final chapter. “Dune: Part Three” opens Dec. 18, the same day as Marvel’s “Avengers: Doomsday” and both will have enough presales to qualify, should their studios choose to enter. The hurdle is the calendar. Motion picture nomination ballots go out to voters Nov. 24 and are due back Dec. 4, and Dec. 2 is the final date for film press conferences and uploads to the Globes’ screening platform. In practical terms, either movie would have to show itself to the several hundred voting journalists more than two weeks before opening day. Based on how Marvel has handled prerelease screenings in the past, I wouldn’t expect “Doomsday” to open its doors that early. “Dune 3” is far more likely to play in those stakes. So in other words, don’t assume anything.

	Another development worth watching for is several studios are taking their animated feature contenders seriously enough to push well beyond that single category.

	Laika is gearing up for a huge push behind Travis Knight’s “Wildwood,” and the stop-motion studio isn’t settling for an animated feature nom. It’s trying to change the conversation around animated movies, which too often get dismissed as “kids’ fare.” At 132 minutes, “Wildwood” is billed as the longest stop-motion feature ever made and it’s Laika’s first PG-13 release. After a Telluride conversation earlier this month with Knight and six-time Oscar-nominated cinematographer Caleb Deschanel, the studio previewed selected scenes at SCAD AnimationFest last week. The film world premieres at the BFI London Film Festival on Oct. 11, then opens AFI Fest as its U.S. premiere on Oct. 21, two days before Fathom Entertainment releases it in theaters. Sources tell Variety that in addition to animated feature, Laika plans to submit “Wildwood” for best picture (drama). The Globes reopened their top categories to animation in 2021, but the three animated films to win a top Globe (“Beauty and the Beast,” “The Lion King” and “Toy Story 2” ) all did it in comedy/musical, long before that. A drama bid is new terrain, but it also sends the message: take animation seriously.

	And Laika does have some Globes history on its side with “Missing Link” pulling off an upset win for animated feature in 2020, coincidentally over “Toy Story 4,” which ultimately won the Oscar.

	“Wildwood” won’t be alone. Independent Film Company’s “Tangles,” Leah Nelson’s hand-drawn adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir about her mother’s Alzheimer’s, is also expected to vie in drama. The biographical Cannes sensation boasts a powerhouse producing team that includes Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Seth Rogen (destined to be an acting nominee for “The Invite”).

	Every placement will ripple into the lead acting races, which the Globes also split by genre. If “Hail Mary” goes comedy, Gosling heads to the side of the house where he won his only Globe, for “La La Land.” A comedy/musical run for “Michael” gives Jackson’s screen debut a friendlier lane than drama, which is filling up fast.



	

					Robert Pattinson in “Primetime,” “The Odyssey,” “Dune: Part Three” and “The Drama”
									A24 / Universal Pictures / Warner Bros.
	



	Start with Robert Pattinson, who has four movies in theaters this year — “The Drama,” “The Odyssey,” “Primetime” and “Dune: Part Three.” How many noms can he collect? For now, his turn as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen in Lance Oppenheim’s “Primetime” looks like his easiest path, in actor (drama), with “The Odyssey” offering another option in supporting actor alongside his co-star John Leguizamo. The front-runners in the actor (drama) category are Andrew Scott, playing the late Ian Charleson in Simon Stone’s “Elsinore” and Pattinson’s “Odyssey” co-star Matt Damon. Behind them, John Turturro (“The Only Living Pickpocket in New York”), Pedro Pascal (“Behemoth!”), Sebastian Stan (“Fjord”) and Anthony Ippolito (“I Play Rocky”) will fight for spots.

	Pattinson isn’t the only big name with more than one ticket to the Hollywood party. Penélope Cruz is also in the hunt with two possible supporting actress bids, for “The Invite” and “La Bola Negra,” plus an actress (drama) play for Florian Zeller’s “Bunker,” opposite her real-life husband, Javier Bardem, who could join her with a drama actor nom of his own.

	Wilde should find enough room for her performance in “The Invite,” in addition to a directing nom for it as well. Perhaps even a third, in supporting actress for “Behemoth!” if it catches on. What a year for her.

	Hüller, meanwhile, can double up in drama actress with “Fatherland” and “Rose,” and she has a path in supporting actress for “Project Hail Mary” (and I guess “Digger?”). Nothing in the Globes rules stops a performer from landing two, three or four noms in the same year.

	We’re also always looking for the Globes picks that come out of nowhere and breathe life into a campaign many had underestimated. Could Gemma Chan or Channing Tatum start supporting runs for Beth de Araújo’s “Josephine?” Could Globes favorite Scarlett Johansson get one going for James Gray’s “Paper Tiger?” And I keep circling Merritt Wever in “Primetime” as a possible nom-morning shocker. It would be well deserved.

	Variety’s predictions in every film category follow below. Not all category placements are confirmed, and all are subject to change.

	The 84th Golden Globe nominations will be announced Monday, Dec. 7, with the ceremony, hosted by Nikki Glaser, set for Sunday, Jan. 10, 2027.

	Projected nomination leaders (films): “The Odyssey” (10); “The Debut” (7); “The Invite” and “La Bola Negra” (6); “Wild Horse Nine” (5); “Dune: Part Three,” “Fjord” and “Michael” (4)

	The list of Oscar predictions in all categories can be found here.

	Variety parent company Penske Media Corporation owns Golden Globes producer Dick Clark Prods. in a joint venture with Eldridge.

title: Florence Pugh Says ‘Instagram Censored Me’ Over Cornell 7 Posts Addressing Sexual Assault Case: ‘Another Shock That Women Are Censored’
description: Florence Pugh‘s press tour for Netflix’s “East of Eden” brought her to “The View,” where co-host Sara Haines brought up the Oscar nominee’s recent s
body:
Florence Pugh‘s press tour for Netflix’s “East of Eden” brought her to “The View,” where co-host Sara Haines brought up the Oscar nominee’s recent social media posts speaking out on the sexual assault case at Cornell University.

	“Even in modern times, women have to bear the consequences of sexual violence, like the allegations currently playing out with the so-called Cornell 7,” Haines said. “The case is still pending, and some of the accused have denied any wrongdoing, but I saw what you wrote about this. This was really important for you. Can you explain why you felt the need to speak up?”
	

	“Rape is something that lives. The fear of it lives in our bodies, and when stories like this come out and it’s really not picked up in the way that you hope it’s picked up, it makes me feel scared, it makes me feel anxious, it made me feel so much rage,” Pugh answered. “I’m lucky enough to do what I do and I have a platform and I wanted to talk about it.”


	Pugh is one of the most prominent celebrities condemning the Cornell 7, the name given online to the seven male students accused of drugging and gang raping their female classmate at Cornell University in October 2024. The woman is now suing her alleged assaulters as well as their fraternity, Cornell University, her former sorority and more. According to the woman’s attorney, Cornell’s original investigation into the alleged crime resulted in only two of the accused men being expelled. The other students received lesser sanctions, such as temporary suspensions, workshops or essay-writing assignments.
	

	“East of Eden” star Pugh, who will next be seen on the big screen in “Avengers: Doomsday” and “Dune: Part Three,” originally posted about the Cornell University sexual assault case in an Instagram post that the social media platform covered with a content warning that read: “This post contains content that some people may find upsetting.” Pugh put up a second post calling out Instagram for “blocking” her statement. As of the publication of this story, Instagram is only blocking Pugh’s second post with a content warning. The actor’s first post is available to see on the platform (see photo below).

	“I’m able to come here and talk about it in real life, even though, sadly, Instagram censored me when I said it, which is also just another shock that women are censored, even when they go through these things, they can’t talk about it,” Pugh said about Instagram. “I feel very lucky and honored that we get to talk about this today. Thank you for bringing it up. It’s an ongoing conversation and it will always be an ongoing conversation until we’re harder on those that do that to women.”

	In her original post on Instagram, Pugh described the alleged sexual assault incident as an “horrific act,” adding that she knew “this has happened before, and I hate the idea of it happening again.” She also urged men to speak out and to be “leading conversations about how we change the allowance and complicity of this behavior as much as we are. Be angry for us. Please.”

	“This is really the moment where we need our men to be as horrified and as sickened as us,” the actor added.

	Pugh added her in second post: “Instagram decided to block my post from getting in front of the right people. Tut tut tut. Oh dear. That doesn’t look great does it? Here’s another go at it in case you were one of those people that can no longer see my post.”

	After Pugh’s post, several other celebrities such as Mariska Hargitay, Josh Gad, Hudson Williams and more used social media to also condemn the Cornell 7. “Arrest them,” wrote “Heated Rivalry” star Williams on his Instagram story while sharing a photo of the seven accused men. “Fuck them and fuck Cornell, too!”

	“We refuse for this victim to be reduced to just another story. Cornell has failed to protect its students,” Hargitay posted on her Instagram in a shared statement with the Joyful Heart Foundation, the organization she founded to support victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, and child abuse.

schema.headline: Florence Pugh Says ‘Instagram Censored Me’ Over Cornell 7 Posts Addressing Sexual Assault Case: ‘Another Shock That Women Are Censored’

title: ’24 Jump Street,’ Hugh Jackman’s ‘Treasure Island’ Remake Get Holiday 2027 Release Dates
description: Sony has slated the highly anticipated comedy sequel “24 Jump Street” and Ridley Scott’s “Treasure Island” remake starring Hugh Jackman for release
body:
Sony has slated the highly anticipated comedy sequel “24 Jump Street” and Ridley Scott’s “Treasure Island” remake starring Hugh Jackman for release around the 2027 holiday season. “Treasure Island” hits theaters first on Nov. 11, 2027, while “24 Jump Street” releases on Dec. 10, 2027.

	Variety exclusively revealed in June that “24 Jump Street” was in the works, with stars Jonah Hill, Channing Tatum and Ice Cube in talks to return for the franchise’s third installment. Rodney Rothman (“Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse”) will serve as director and co-wrote the script with Hill and Meghan Malloy. Phil Lord and Chris Miller — who helmed 2012’s “21 Jump Street” and 2014’s “22 Jump Street” — are returning as producers. Neal H. Moritz. Tatum and Reid Carolin are also producing for Free Association, along with Hill and Matt Dines under their Strong Baby banner.
	

	Also in June, it was revealed that Jackman and Scott were teaming up to adapt Robert Louis Stevenson’s classic swashbuckling tale for the big screen. Scott will direct “Treasure Island” with a screenplay by Emmy-winning “Adolescence” writer Jack Thorne. Scott also serves as producer with Michael Pruss for his Scott Free banner. Thorne will executive produce “Treasure Island.”


	Sony also dated Roshan Sethi’s thriller “The Surgeon” for April 2, 2027, and the coming-of-age comedy “Narcs” for Aug. 20, 2027. Michelle Yeoh stars in “The Surgeon” as a skilled doctor who is kidnapped and forced to operate on a mysterious patient. “Narcs” stars Mason Thames, and plot details remain under wraps. John Phillips, who wrote “No Hard Feelings” and “Dirty Grandpa,” makes his directorial debut with the project.
	

	Two films also got their release dates shifted. “Grandgear,” from “Godzilla Minus One” director Takashi Yamazaki, was set to debut on Feb. 18, 2028, but will now drop on Jan. 14, 2028. “Helldivers,” based on the popular video game series, was set for release on Nov. 10, 2027. Sony pushed the title to June 9, 2028.

schema.headline: ’24 Jump Street,’ Hugh Jackman’s ‘Treasure Island’ Remake Get Holiday 2027 Release Dates

title: SCP Foundation Anthology Movie in the Works at Neon, Based on Online Horror Forum
description: Neon is developing an anthology movie based on the community-driven horror forum The SCP Foundation. The project, which will focus on platforming em
body:
Neon is developing an anthology movie based on the community-driven horror forum The SCP Foundation. The project, which will focus on platforming emerging filmmakers, is slated for release in 2027.

	The SCP Wiki, created in 2008, is a collaborative speculative fiction website where users submit written works that expand the lore of the SCP Foundation, a secret organization that collects and studies supernatural and often highly dangerous objects and entities for the good of humanity. Some of the most popular entries include SCP-173, a concrete statue that attacks anyone who breaks eye contact, and SCP-682, a supremely intelligent reptile that can adapt to any environment and rapidly heal any injury.
	

	In Neon’s release, the studio made a point to emphasize that it is releasing the film under the Creative Commons license CC BY-SA and has been in communication with the SCP Wiki team about adapting its works. Neon’s announcement comes after the SCP Wiki team denounced a film from A24, Spooky Pictures and Image Nation shortly after it was unveiled. After the A24 film was announced, the SCP team wrote in a statement, “We have not had any communication with the filmmakers, producers, or distributors for this project, despite our best efforts, and to the best of our knowledge they have not made any efforts to contact us. Furthermore, A24 does not and cannot have any exclusive rights to anything related to the SCP Foundation, including any films that Spooky Pictures or anyone else may choose to create.”


	Internet IP went from pariah to pay dirt in Hollywood after the success of A24’s “Backrooms,” based on the web series by 21-year-old Kane Parsons, who wrote and directed the film. After the horror-thriller grossed $400 million against a $10 million budget, Warner Bros. scooped up film rights for Trevor Henderson’s viral horror creation Siren Head and attached Brian Duffield as director and Zach Cregger as the writer. TriStar Pictures acquired another one of Henderson’s creatures, Cartoon Cat, for a movie adaptation in the weeks after.

title: David Ellison Taps Mattel’s Ynon Kreiz to Be Co-CEO of Merged Paramount-Warner Bros.
description: Ynon Kreiz, who is stepping down as CEO of Mattel after eight years, will join David Ellison’s Paramount — which is expected to close its mega-merge
body:
Ynon Kreiz, who is stepping down as CEO of Mattel after eight years, will join David Ellison’s Paramount — which is expected to close its mega-merger with Warner Bros. Discovery on Oct. 6 — as co-CEO of the new company, Paramount announced.

	As chairman and CEO, Ellison will lead all strategy, creative and technology functions. Kreiz, as co-CEO, will oversee the company’s day-to-day operations and integration of the combined businesses. It’s a “pairing that joins complementary skillsets to amplify results,” Paramount said in announcing the appointment Wednesday. The businesses of the combined company (whose name has not yet been announced) will report jointly to both Ellison and Kreiz.
	

	Kreiz will start at Paramount on Oct. 5, 2026, as co-CEO. He also will join the company’s board of directors. 


	News of Kreiz’s hiring came shortly after Paramount cleared the final step before it could close the $111 billion Warner Bros. Discovery merger when a judge approved the company’s settlement of the antitrust lawsuit brought by 12 state attorneys general. The merger is expected to close Oct. 6, according to Paramount regulatory filings.

	Ellison’s appointment of Kreiz “caps a long-term plan: pursue both Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, then partner with a leading executive of his caliber to integrate, operationalize and manage the businesses as they build one of the most ambitious next-generation media companies in the industry’s history,” according to Paramount’s announcement.

	One source close to the situation told Variety said that Ellison’s courting of Kreiz has been in the works for months and was “another ace up Ellison’s sleeve.”
	

	Ellison, in a companywide memo Wednesday about Kreiz’s appointment, wrote, “We still have work to do before the [Warner Bros.] deal closes, and nothing changes until it does. But I wanted you to hear this from me first. I hope you’re as excited as I am to welcome Ynon to our leadership team.”

	Ellison said in a statement: “Bringing together Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery to create a next-generation global media company is a transformational moment for our industry. Leading it takes a rare combination of strategic vision, operational depth and experience running a public company at the highest levels of media. Ynon brings all three. In Ynon, I’m adding a partner with strong leadership and the operating firepower this integration demands. It’s a division of labor built on our complementary strengths, with clear reporting lines and it lets me focus where I can contribute most: long-term strategy, the company’s overall creative direction, talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation. We’re like-minded, we see this business the same way and there’s no one I’d rather partner with. Together we’ll build one integrated company that is creator-first, tech-forward and built to scale globally.”

	Kreiz said in a statement provided by Paramount: “I’m excited to partner with David to build the next-generation media and entertainment company — bringing together premium content and iconic brands at the highest quality and scale, serving global audiences across every entertainment vertical and distribution platform. David is a unique talent and executive: a rare blend of business acumen, creative instinct, and clear vision. I very much share that vision, and I’m inspired by what we can accomplish together. The industry is at an inflection point, demanding evolution, investment, and a willingness to rethink business models. I look forward to working with the leadership team to build a cohesive global entertainment platform — one that stands out with best-in-class operations and execution powered by technology, with unparalleled creative relationships, production capabilities, and global reach. We will continue empowering creators, make this company a greenfield for innovation and storytelling, and collaborate with key partners to reach and engage fans worldwide.”
	

	Gerry Cardinale, founder and managing partner of RedBird Capital Partners — Paramount’s co-controlling shareholder and a member of its board of directors — praised Ellison’s ability to lead the company through two “historic acquisitions.” In August 2025, Skydance Media closed the deal to acquire Paramount Global. Cardinale added that Ellison has at the same time been “running the business and building a team that’s already exceeding our synergy targets, beating our financial metrics, and never wavering on our commitment to the creative community.”

	Mattel earlier Wednesday announced that Kreiz will step down as chairman and CEO effective Oct. 2, “to take a senior leadership position at another public company.” Roger Lynch, Condé Nast’s CEO, has been named Mattel’s next CEO.

	Kreiz, a veteran media exec, is the former chairman and CEO of Maker Studios, a YouTube-oriented digital content network acquired by Disney in 2014. Kreiz exited Disney in 2016 and joined Mattel in 2018. From 2008-11, he served as chairman and CEO of Endemol Group, and before that was a general partner at venture-capital firm Balderton Capital (formerly Benchmark Capital Europe) from 2005-07. Earlier in his career, Kreiz co-founded and was chairman and CEO of Fox Kids Europe.

	Mattel has credited Kreiz with boosting its market share across key toy categories, ranking No. 1 globally in dolls, vehicles, and infant, toddler and preschool segments. Mattel also noted that Kreiz oversaw Mattel Studios’ first theatrical release, “Barbie” starring Margot Robbie, which was the top global box office film of 2023 and has stood as Warner Bros. Pictures’ highest-grossing movie of all time.

	Said Cardinale, “Ynon has spent his career at the intersection of media, technology and franchise-building — pairing extraordinary storytelling with the technology to deliver it to fans everywhere. He understands not just how fans connect with the IP they love, but the economics that make entertainment endure. Great leaders accomplish great things. Historic ones know when to bring in the right partner to make it last — and that’s what David has done. It’s exactly why the company will have the operational firepower and the cutting-edge leadership to win.”

	Along with Kreiz, the leadership of the combined Paramount-WBD is already taking shape. Casey Bloys, head of WBD’s HBO, is poised to assume oversight of the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. streaming business after Cindy Holland announced Tuesday she was stepping down from her role running Paramount+ and other direct-to-consumer.

schema.headline: David Ellison Taps Mattel’s Ynon Kreiz to Be Co-CEO of Merged Paramount-Warner Bros.

            Cornell has agreed to an independent investigation that will look into the way the University handled the alleged 2024 gang rape of a female student.
      
    
            New York Governor Kathy Hochul called for the probe, and she tells ABC News the Ivy League school is on board.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She told the outlet ... "I wanted to make sure they knew how important this was, and they absolutely agreed. And they're acting on this this afternoon."
      
    
            Hochul says the point of the investigation is to determine whether or not the University did all it could to protect its student.
      

            She said ... "People need to know the truth and I think it's important for the public, for the victim, her family and the University community to know that their University did everything that they're supposed to do."
      
    
            Hochul insists the way in which women are treated on college campuses needs to change.
      
    
            This comes after Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten reopened the case ... in the wake of Jane Doe's civil suit alleging she was drugged and sexually assaulted by 7 members of the Chi Phi fraternity.

description:
Bill Cosby

body:
Bill Cosby
                          Allegedly No Shows 3rd Deposition
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 30, 2026
                            4:11 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Bill Cosby allegedly failed to show up for a deposition in a civil lawsuit he's facing ... and his legal adversaries are telling the judge it's the third one he's missed ... and they want him to face some serious consequences.
      
    
            According to legal documents filed by the lawyers for several women who are suing the disgraced actor and comedian, Bill was scheduled to be deposed from September 22 to September 24 ... but they say Cosby unilaterally canceled on September 21 ... despite receiving proper notice of the dates he was to be deposed.
      
    
            They claim this is the third time they've had dates set for a deposition that Cosby's team has called off at the last minute ... citing an instance in April and another in June. 
      
    
            And now the plaintiffs are asking the court to hit him with serious sanctions or, at the very least, an order blocking him from testifying so he "cannot benefit from his delay tactics."
      

            We broke the story ... Cosby's legal team filed documents in July claiming he was simply too sick to sit for a deposition. His team says he had to cancel the dates in June because his male assistant -- who helps with his basic needs like using the restroom -- wasn't available. Cosby is 89 years old.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As you know ... in a separate case, Donna Motsinger was awarded $19.25 million and an additional $40 million in punitive damages after she successfully sued Cosby for sexual assault and sexual battery. He filed for a new trial, but the court denied it.
      
    
            We've reached out to Cosby ... so far, no word back.
